title: Protocol-complete Stack
prompt:
Implement `class Stack` that supports:

- `push(x)`, `pop()` (raise `IndexError` on empty), `peek()` (raise `IndexError` on empty)
- `len(stack)`, `stack[i]` (int indexing, negative included), `x in stack`, iteration (bottom→top)
- slicing: `stack[1:3]` returns a NEW Stack
- `__eq__` against another Stack comparing element order (return NotImplemented for non-Stack)
- `__repr__` as `Stack(<items joined by ', '>)`

tests.name: core operations
tests.code:
s = Stack()
s.push(1); s.push(2)
assert s.pop() == 2
assert s.peek() == 1
assert len(s) == 1
empty = Stack()
try:
    empty.pop()
except IndexError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('pop on empty must raise IndexError')
print('ok')
tests.hint: list-based storage is fine; just obey the protocol signatures.

tests.name: sequence protocol incl. slicing
tests.code:
s = Stack([10, 20, 30])
assert 20 in s
assert [x for x in s] == [10, 20, 30]
assert s[1] == 20 and s[-1] == 30
sliced = s[0:2]
assert isinstance(sliced, Stack) and list(sliced) == [10, 20]
assert s == Stack([10, 20, 30])
assert (s == [10, 20, 30]) is False
assert repr(s) == 'Stack(10, 20, 30)'
print('ok')
tests.hint: __getitem__ must accept both int and slice; return NotImplemented (not False) for foreign types in __eq__.
